name: single_cylinder_engine_weibe
title: Single-cylinder engine with Weibe combustion (crank-angle dynamic)
summary: Crank-angle-resolved model of one cylinder of a four-stroke spark-ignition engine: the cylinder pressure, gas mass, combustion heat release (Weibe function in a PROCEDURE), wall heat losses and piston work are integrated with INTEGRAL over the intake stroke (-360 to -180 deg), with a choked intake flow through the intake valve and the charge modelled as a single ideal gas with constant gamma.

authors: TBD (ULiège engine thermodynamics course exercise, 2008-2009; author not identified in the source)
origin.course: ULiège, engine thermodynamics, Weibe combustion model, repetition 4 (2008-2009)

verification.reference: None available (no .sol file and no original EES file, searched in ~/Nextcloud/thermo_models and in CoolSolve misc/EES_ok.zip): reproduction of the CoolSolve example solution (75/75 scalar variables bit-identical) and of the value committed in the CoolSolve regression test for that example (tests/test_examples.cpp, p = 89221.7 Pa), plus CoolSolve solution check (0 residual) and geometric / choked-flow sanity checks
verification.notes: Status runs (no independent reference): the example solution and the library model are bit-identical, so max_rel_diff = 0. Final p 89221.7 Pa, T 276.14 K (absolute temperature, see README), W_tot 59.76 J. Sanity checks: 67/67 equations satisfied with max |residual| 0, RK4 180 accepted/0 rejected steps of 1 deg, V(theta) matches the closed-form slider-crank volume at the 37 trajectory rows, M_dot equals the isentropic choked flow 0.10193 kg/s only between the valve angles and while p < p_out.

related_external: CoolSolve examples/engine_weibe_cycle.eescode (same model, kept in CoolSolve as a test case)
